textbookText: The graph indicates that the volume of gas is zero at -2730C =0 kelvin. In 1848 Lord Kelvin identified the temperature (-2730C) (more exact value -273.15 0C) as theoretically the lowest attainable temperature called as absolute zero. Then a new scale called an absolute temperature scale was developed with absolute zero as the starting point. Absolute zero =-273.15 0C ≈ -273 0C is a theoretical temperature because volume of gas can be measured practically only over a certain range of temperature. At very low temperature gas condenses to liquid. where P1>P2>P3 Fig: Plot of volume vs temperature at different pressures By convention, we use T to denote absolute (kelvin) temperature and t to indicate temperature on the Celsius scale. They are interconvertible to each other using the relationship: T=t0C + 273.15 It means the boiling point of water (1000C) = (100+273.15)=373.15K in Kelvin scale. If the volume of a given amount of gas is constant, pressure is directly proportional to temperature. P∝ T or P=KT Or P1/T1=P2/T2 This relationship is another form of Charle’s law which is also called Gay-Lussac’s law
